text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Direct quotations from the article with paragraph citations, e.g., \"None of the cars developed so far are completely driverless...\" (7) and \"Presently, traffic laws are written...\" (9)", "quality": "Textual evidence integration", "description": "The essay grounds its claims in specific quoted passages from the source article with citations, rather than relying on paraphrase or general recollection."}, {"evidence": "Organized into distinct body paragraphs each devoted to one argument (not fully driverless; safety/liability concerns) with a clear thesis and conclusion", "quality": "Structured organization", "description": "The essay presents a clear thesis and develops each supporting point in its own focused paragraph, building logically toward a conclusion."}, {"evidence": "Develops the liability question — \"who is at fault - the driver or the manufacturer?\" — and explores its implications for safety and controversy", "quality": "Analytical depth", "description": "The essay pushes beyond surface claims to examine consequences and complications, such as the legal and accountability problems raised by driverless cars."}, {"evidence": "Consistent formal register maintained throughout, with few informal or conversational digressions", "quality": "Consistent formal tone", "description": "The essay sustains an academic voice and avoids the informal asides and rhetorical questions that weaken the other essay's authority."}, {"evidence": "Each paragraph connects back to the thesis that driverless cars are unsafe and not fully functional, with topic sentences previewing each point", "quality": "Coherent argumentative focus", "description": "The essay keeps every paragraph tied to its central position, with clear topic sentences and transitions that reinforce the overall argument."}]}
